This Brabus G-Wagen 6x6 Deserves Nothing but Respect!
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | brabus
Another day, another tuned G-Wagen from the model’s second generation? Well, yes and no. Yes because it did come from a renowned tuner’s portfolio, and no because it is more of a coachbuilt model rather than a modified one.
As we are certain you already know, the modern-day Mercedes G-Wagen is not offered with six axles, regardless of whether we are talking about a normal Benz or the range-topping Mercedes-AMG G 63. But its predecessor was available in this configuration straight from the factory, looking like an apocalypse-ready vehicle that can conquer the outdoors like a veritable off-roading champ.
Christened the Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6x6 , because the Affalterbach sub-brand was not fully integrated into Mercedes back then, it saw the light of day between 2013 and 2015. Production took place at the Magna Steyr factory in Graz, Austria, and this model was a four-door pickup truck with six axles. It had a front engine and six-wheel drive layout, packing a 5.5-liter twin-turbocharged V8 mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission.
The mill was rated at 536 hp (544 ps/400 kW) and 561 lb-ft (761 Nm) of torque, enabling 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in around eight seconds, and a maximum speed limited to 100 mph (160 kph). Thus, it wasn’t exactly a sprinter disguised as a triathlete, but then again, it did have a curb weight exceeding 4 metric tons (9,000 lbs), and measure a massive 231.3 inches (5,875 mm) in length, 87 inches (2,210 mm) in height, and 83.1 inches (2,110 mm) in width.
Photo: Instagram | brabus As for the Mercedes- AMG G 63 6x6 pictured above, it came from Brabus, and it is called the XLP 6x6 Adventure . It has an upgraded 4.0-liter bi-turbo V8 that produces 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque. The engine allows it to hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 5.8 seconds, and the maximum top speed is 130 mph (210 kph).
Based on the modern-day Mercedes-AMG G 63, the Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure is a four-door pickup truck with front and rear fender extensions, a roll bar, carbon side walls in the load area, underride guard, skirts at the front and rear, some carbon-made panel parts on the sides, electric running boards, LED lighting, and even a winch with a 4.5-ton (9,921 lbs) capacity, and a plastic cable that is 30 meters (98 feet) in length.
Additional lights, a wind deflector, a roof rack, and other things are also on deck, and this Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure comes with 9.5x22-inch wheels on all axles, shod in 325/55 tires. The pictured example has a glossy black look, some red details in the Panamericana grille that is decorated with the Brabus logo, a red winch cable, red calipers and suspension, red logos on the sides, wheels, and rear, and a few other goodies. And yes, portal axles are also part of the makeover.
More red accents can be seen on the inside, and these include the trim on the steering wheel, the 12 o’clock marker, the door pins, window and seat controls, air vents, speaker covers, and other things. The leather upholstery is black and has a diamond pattern, there is some extra carbon fiber trim, and we can also see some overhead gauges, as well as a black headliner, and other things that further contribute to the special nature of this heavily modified Mercedes-AMG G 63.
Photo: Instagram | brabus According to the official specs, this model is 243.4 inches (6,183 mm) long, 90.3 inches (2,293 mm) tall, and 86.3 inches (2,192 mm) wide, and tips the scales at over 8,000 pounds net (3,670 kg). It burns the equivalent of 10.7 mpg US (21.9 l/100 km) combined, so it’s not exactly a frugal ride, but then again, you didn’t think it was, did you? As for the average carbon dioxide emissions, these are rated at 420 g/km.
While the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63 has an MSRP of $198,750 attached to it in the United States of America for the 2027 model year, the Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure is a seven-digit affair. We found the pictured example advertised on the tuner’s official website with an asking price of 1,333,774.61 euros attached to it at the time of writing, and this equals almost $1.5 million at the current exchange rate.
This build is definitely a masterpiece aimed at deep-pocketed enthusiasts, and while it can cope with the great outdoors like a champ, the chances of encountering one of these off the beaten path are close to zero. That’s because this model will mostly be used as a school bus and grocery getter for the most part, and it’s sad, because it deserves to be put through its paces on challenging terrains.
Still, if you paid $1.5 million for your very own Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure, would you really take it off-roading? And more importantly, would you ever see yourself owning one of these if money were the least of your worries? I would! View this post on Instagram A post shared by BRABUS (@brabus)
